routing.reason: Input validation and error handling in one small API file (src/app.ts, src/tasks.ts), a one-line client fix in public/app.js, and tests; the ticket already lists testable acceptance criteria.
rulings: Ruling: workflow default, not hotfix — a validation bug with a clear fix, not an urgent outage — cost if wrong: one extra plan gate to approve

Ruling: skip frame (po) — the ticket already lists 7 testable acceptance criteria, framing would only repeat them — cost if wrong: an edge case (e.g. PATCH with a non-string title, 400 on a missing task id vs 404 order) is decided by the implementer
Ruling: no prd, architecture, ux, seo — no vague scope, no cross-cutting decision, the page keeps its existing error element (#error), no public page metadata change — cost if wrong: none expected

Ruling: security review at medium effort — input parsing and error leakage (criterion 5) are touched, but the app has no auth, payments or personal data — cost if wrong: a missed leak path such as a body-size or non-object JSON body (e.g. `null` or an array) reaching the handlers

Ruling: budget $0.70 — S change of 3 source files plus tests, covering plan, one implement round, one review round and the security review — cost if wrong: run stops before its reviews and needs a budget increase

Ruling: no squads declared — the lead plans the whole ticket; back takes src/app.ts, src/tasks.ts and test/tasks.test.ts, front takes the one-line check in public/app.js (form submit must catch the API error and call show())

first: test/tasks.test.ts(96,74): error TS7006: Parameter 't' implicitly has an 'any' type.

criteria.why: createTask calls validateTitle, which rejects missing, empty, blank and non-string titles with 400 'title is required'; validation runs before the insert. Tests cover {}, '', '   ', 123 and null.
PATCH validates when body.title !== undefined, and updateTask validates again. null is rejected as well. Tests cover bad PATCH titles and check that the task is unchanged.
The title is trimmed and then checked against 200 characters, with the exact error message. The saved value is the trimmed one. Tests cover 201, 200 and padded 200.
readJson turns JSON.parse failures into HttpError(400, 'invalid JSON body'). It also rejects null, arrays and primitives, which is slightly beyond the ticket but sensible. Tests cover POST and PATCH.
The catch handler sends HttpError messages as-is. Anything else is logged with console.error and answered with 500 'internal error'. A test breaks the DB and checks the response and the log call.
The submit handler wraps the call in try/catch and calls show(err). This assumes api() throws an Error carrying the API's message, which the diff doesn't show. No UI test.
New tests cover every server-side case. The UI change is untested, but that is reasonable for this project.

findings.what: Title validation runs twice on PATCH: once in app.ts and again in updateTask. The call in app.ts is redundant, and the second call re-trims.

The server doesn't treat non-integer ids or oversized bodies specially, and PATCH `done` isn't validated. These were out of scope for the ticket, so this is only a note. Separately, a non-boolean `done` could still reach SQLite.
The 500 test relies on dropping the table from a second connection. It works, but it is somewhat heavyweight and fragile. The front-end error display has no test.
readJson also rejects valid JSON that isn't an object (null, arrays, numbers) with 'invalid JSON body'. This goes slightly past the ticket, but it prevents a crash on `body.title`.

judge.summary: The diff meets every acceptance criterion. It adds a small HttpError class and a shared validateTitle, hides internal error messages behind a logged 500, and makes the page show API errors. The tests are thorough and include a real 500 path. The only issues are minor: PATCH validates the title twice, and the UI change has no test.
